thread:
Alex R.: kicking off PRD checklist for generation edge-cases we need covered before beta launch. focus: streaming resume, truncation semantics, token accounting, and retry idempotency. draft acceptance criteria below, pls 👍 or call out gaps.

Maya Chen: thanks — can we make truncation behavior deterministic across hosted/dedicated/private? i.e., same 'truncated' flag and reason codes. customers keep hitting mismatch between dev/prod.

Samir Patel: +1. also need explicit policy for partial-chunk resume: do we support resume-by-offset or only resume-by-prefix (delta tokens)?

Jordan K: preference for resume-by-prefix with resume_token to avoid offset fragility. resume_token = opaque cursor, server validates kv-cache compatibility. if cache mismatch -> full re-gen fallback.

Priya Gupta: customer ask: enterprise wants guaranteed no data leakage when fallback to smaller model on overload. requirement: fallback must be same-safety-profile (no docs access). add to acceptance criteria.

Alex R.: acceptance criteria draft: 1) streaming responses include resume_token on every chunk boundary; 2) client can POST /resume with resume_token + context_len header; 3) server returns status: resumed|incompatible|expired; 4) truncation reasons standardized: length_limit, safety_cut, user_cancel, rate_limit; 5) token accounting reported per-chunk and reconciled on resume; 6) retries must be idempotent for safe endpoints (function-calls) and non-duplicative for generation.

Maya Chen: small nit: include 'partial_repeat' reason when resume shows repeated tokens due to overlap. also define TTL for resume_token (e.g., 5 minutes) and max resumable tokens (e.g., 8192).

Samir Patel: edge-case: client reconnects and resumes but model version changed (rollout). we need policy: if model_version != token.version -> treat as incompatible and surface clear metrics. also track fallback-routing attribution.

Jordan K: implementation note: resume_token = HMAC(model_version, kv_root_hash, last_prefix_hash, expiry) so we can verify locally without state. avoids large server-side session store.

Priya Gupta: acceptance test ideas: - simulate resume after 2 min and confirm identical tail tokens when model unchanged - simulate model swap and expect incompatible + deterministic fallback - simulate truncated safety_cut and verify truncated flag + audit log + redaction where required

Alex R.: good tests. now token accounting: on truncated responses we must bill for emitted tokens only, but also surface potential additional compute cost if we aborted mid-synthesis (estimate on server). add a field billing_estimate in the final chunk.

Maya Chen: retry semantics: define idempotency-key behavior. for streaming endpoints, client should attach Idempotency-Key for whole request stream. if retry receives duplicate key and same params -> server should attempt resume/fork detection, else return 409 with guidance.

Samir Patel: client guidance doc snippet: ```
// pseudocode
POST /v1/generate
Headers: Idempotency-Key: <uuid>, Resume-Token: <opt>
Body: {prompt, max_tokens}
```

Jordan K: also need rate-limit backpressure: if server queues beyond X ms, return 202 queued with eta and a retry-after header instead of accepting and then truncating mid-stream. reduces weird resumptions.

Priya Gupta: launch blockers from security: confirm resume_token cannot leak sensitive context (no PII inside), HMAC-only checksums ok. add KMS rotation plan for signing keys.

Alex R.: action items: Maya to finalize enum of truncation reasons + codes (due EOD), Samir to write resume_token spec + security notes (tomorrow), Jordan to prototype HMAC verification and queue behavior (this week), Priya to draft enterprise acceptance tests and legal note (3 days). I'll consolidate into PRD draft and ping for review.
